source.name: UCI Online Retail II
source.series_used: United Kingdom daily net revenue, trading calendar

decisions: Invoices prefixed 'C' are cancellations. A cancellation is a reversal of an earlier sale, not a sale, so it is removed rather than netted: netting would attribute a return to the day it was processed instead of the day it was sold.
Non-positive quantity outside a cancellation is an adjustment or a data error. Removed; it cannot represent demand.
Non-positive price rows are samples, write-offs and manual corrections. Removed from revenue, since a zero-priced line is not a sale at any value.
Rows without a customer id are retained. They are guest checkouts and dropping them would bias revenue downward by roughly a fifth.
31 trading days are absent (public holidays inside a trading week). Linearly interpolated so the seasonal decomposition has a regular index; they are a 4.9% share of the series.

T2B_decomposition.note: Countries as segments, on the real invoice ledger. The identity is algebraic, so a failure here would mean the adapter, not the method, is wrong.

T2C_null_calibration.caveat: Real windows are not a true null: genuine shocks occur in this data and are not labelled. The empirical rate is therefore an upper bound on the false-positive rate, not an unbiased estimate of it.

seasonal_gate.cost: Every window is refused on this source, including the February to August windows where the raw statistic was well calibrated. The gate is a blunt instrument: it asks whether the declared cycle can be covered, not whether the cycle matters for this particular window. That refinement is not implemented and should not be claimed.
seasonal_gate.benefit: The 27.9% false-positive rate below is what the engine produced BEFORE the gate. After it, the engine issues no verdict at all on this source, so the rate is zero by refusal rather than by accuracy.

seasonally_stable_subset.why: February to August contains no Christmas ramp. If the aggregate failure is caused by an unavailable annual cycle, this subset should be calibrated.

T2D_causal_negative_control.note: No intervention exists at these dates. Every R3 here is a false positive. The threshold is p <= 0.10, so a calibrated test yields about 10%.

T2E_injected_recovery.why_restricted: A power measurement taken across the Christmas ramp measures baseline bias, not power. The windows are drawn from the months where T2-C shows the baseline is sound.
T2E_injected_recovery.note: The shock is synthetic but the noise, seasonality and calendar are real. Bias is the median estimate minus the injected size.
